AYRO is a Round Rock, Texas maker of low-speed electric utility vehicles for campuses, municipalities and commercial fleets, including the AYRO Vanish. Customers are universities, municipalities and fleets, with small revenue. Listed on Nasdaq (AYRO). AYRO was created in 2020 through a merger with DropCar, and builds its vehicles in partnership with Cenntro in China. Models include the Vanish and the 411x, used on campuses, in resorts and for light municipal work. Small-cap EV company with minimal consumer brand awareness.

Bermuda-based life insurance and annuity consolidator that acquires closed books of business in the US, UK and Australia, serving existing policyholders. Backed by Blackstone and Cinven and acquired by Nippon Life of Japan in 2025. The Nippon Life deal, announced in late 2024, valued the group at roughly USD 8.2 billion. Operations include Resolution Life US and an Australian life business bought from AMP in 2020, plus Bermuda reinsurance. B2B financial business with little consumer brand awareness.

Water and sewage utility of the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, based in Belo Horizonte, serving millions of customers in hundreds of municipalities. State-controlled, listed on B3 (CSMG3), and subject to a privatisation process. Customers are households and businesses. Founded in 1963, it is the main water and sewage provider across most of the state, and the Minas Gerais state government holds roughly half of the shares. It also owns the Copanor subsidiary serving the poorer northern region. Moderate regional awareness.

German manufacturer of high-performance gearboxes and drivetrains for tanks, naval vessels and industrial applications, based in Augsburg. Customers are defence ministries and shipbuilders. Relisted on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (R3NK) in 2024. The business was founded in 1873 and is best known for gearboxes fitted to the Leopard 2 battle tank, alongside slide bearings, marine and industrial drives and test systems. It was listed in February 2024 after a long period under private equity and industrial owners. B2B with high profile in defence circles, none with consumers.

UK supermarket chain founded in 1965 and based in Leeds, with around 1,000 stores plus George clothing and online grocery. Owned by Mohsin and Zuber Issa and TDR Capital since 2021. Revenue about GBP 23 billion. Founded in 1965 in Yorkshire, it was owned by Walmart from 1999 until 2021, and Walmart kept a small minority stake. Own-label ranges include Just Essentials and Extra Special, and the group also runs Asda Express convenience stores acquired alongside the EG Group deal. Mass-market consumer brand with very high UK awareness.

US discount retailer based in Goodlettsville, Tennessee, with about 20,000 small-box stores selling basic groceries, household goods and apparel, mostly in rural and small-town communities. Listed on the NYSE (DG). Revenue about USD 40 billion. The company dates to 1939 and now operates in about 48 states, with the pOpshelf concept and DG Market small-format stores alongside its core Dollar General stores. It targets low and fixed-income shoppers within a short drive of home. Strong consumer brand across the US, with motorsport sponsorship.

Pioneering electric vehicle battery-swapping network founded by Shai Agassi, which operated swap stations and electric cars in Israel and Denmark. The company went bankrupt in 2013. Defunct. The company, founded in 2007 and led by Shai Agassi, raised around USD 850 million and used the Renault Fluence Z.E. as its swappable-battery car. It also pursued networks in Australia and elsewhere before filing for bankruptcy in May 2013. It had historical profile in the EV industry but no ongoing consumer presence.

Miami-based primary care provider focused on Medicare Advantage seniors, operating clinics across Florida and other US states. Listed on the NYSE (CANO), it filed for Chapter 11 in 2024 and emerged as a private company. Founded in 2009, it listed in 2021 through a SPAC merger with Jaws Acquisition, and operated clinics in Florida, Texas, Nevada, Illinois and Puerto Rico under the Cano Health and Cano Medical Centers names. Consumer healthcare brand with local awareness.

State-owned Chinese conglomerate based in Hong Kong with retail (CR Vanguard supermarkets), beverages (Snow beer), property, power and pharmaceuticals. Group revenue is in the hundreds of billions of yuan. The group is owned by China's central government. Its businesses include CR Beer, whose Snow brand is among the best-selling beers in the world by volume, the MixC shopping mall chain through China Resources Land, CR Power, CR Pharmaceutical and gas distribution. Consumer brands very well known in China.

Dubai real estate developer DarGlobal, a unit of Dar Al Arkan, developing luxury branded residences such as Trump International projects in Jeddah, Dubai and the Maldives. Listed on London AIM. Customers are wealthy property buyers. The parent, Dar Al Arkan, is a Saudi Arabian developer listed on Tadawul, and DarGlobal markets its branded projects internationally under licences such as Trump and Versace. Brand moderately visible in luxury property.

Irish telecoms operator providing broadband, mobile and TV, formerly Eircom, based in Dublin and owned by NJJ and others. Millions of customers across Ireland. The company is Ireland's incumbent fixed-line operator, owning the national wholesale access network through its Open eir arm, and operates the eir Sport television channels. It has backed Irish rugby and Gaelic games. Well-known consumer brand in Ireland, and a sponsor of rugby and GAA.

US ground freight logistics company based in Greeneville, Tennessee, providing expedited airport-to-airport and last-mile delivery. Listed on Nasdaq (FWRD). Revenue about USD 2.5 billion. It acquired freight forwarder Omni Logistics in January 2024, widening it from airport-to-airport trucking into global forwarding and last-mile services. It was founded in 1981. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Idaho-based lithium-ion battery cell maker for energy storage and electric vehicles, building a battery gigafactory in Arizona. Backed by investors such as Koch. Customers are vehicle makers and utilities. Its planned KOREPlex plant in Buckeye, Arizona is designed to produce cells at gigawatt-hour scale. Backers have included Koch Strategic Platforms. B2B with limited public brand profile.

French arm of the Leasys mobility business, a long-term car rental and leasing company within the FCA Bank group (Stellantis and Credit Agricole). Based in Poissy. Offers leasing and car subscription to companies and individuals. Leasys is the leasing unit of FCA Bank (Stellantis and Credit Agricole), with its parent business in Rome. Its offers include the CarCloud subscription service and Drivalia short-term rental, spread across several European countries. Moderate B2B awareness.

Russia's largest mobile operator, MTS, based in Moscow, with over 80 million subscribers plus banking, media and cloud services. Part of Sistema and listed on the Moscow Exchange; under Western sanctions since 2022. Sistema holds roughly half of MTS. Other businesses include MTS Bank, the KION streaming service and cloud and fintech arms, and it also operates in Armenia. Its American depositary receipts left the NYSE in 2022. Consumer brand with high awareness in Russia.

Macau casino resort operator running Venetian Macao, Parisian Macao, The Londoner Macao and the Four Seasons Macao. Subsidiary of Las Vegas Sands and listed on HKEX (1928). Las Vegas Sands owns the large majority. The company opened Sands Macao in 2004 and Venetian Macao in 2007, and also runs Plaza Macao and the Cotai Arena, which stages concerts and sports events. Consumer-facing luxury entertainment brand with strong regional awareness.

Dubai-based outsourcing and technology services company for governments, processing visa and passport applications in more than 140 countries through its centres. Owned by EQT. It was founded in 2001 in Mumbai and works for dozens of client governments, taking applications, biometrics and document checks on their behalf and charging service fees to applicants. B2B, though travellers encounter the brand at visa centres worldwide.

US lodging real estate investment trust based in Orlando, owning upper-upscale hotels and resorts operated by Marriott, Hyatt and Hilton. Listed on the NYSE (XHR). The trust was spun off from InvenTrust Properties in 2015. Revenue comes from hotel operations, with brands such as Marriott and Hyatt paid fees to manage the properties. B2B investor brand with no consumer name.

Hong Kong fibre broadband and telecom provider, HKBN, serving residential and corporate customers with internet and enterprise solutions. Previously listed on HKEX (1310) and subject to a takeover offer by China Mobile Hong Kong in 2025. HKBN grew from the 1999 start-up City Telecom, bought Wharf T&T in 2017 to build its enterprise arm, and sells 10-gigabit residential fibre plans in Hong Kong. Well-known local consumer brand.

MNT-Halan is an Egyptian fintech group in Cairo formed by combining the Halan motorbike-based mobility business with MNT, led by founder Mounir Nakhla. It offers microfinance and consumer lending, including Tasaheel, to underbanked consumers and small businesses. It became a unicorn in 2022 after a funding round led by Chimera. Strong consumer awareness in Egypt through advertising.

US children's apparel retailer based in Secaucus, New Jersey, selling kids' clothing through roughly 500 stores and online in North America. Listed on Nasdaq (PLCE) and under financial pressure in recent years. Brands are The Children's Place, Gymboree, Sugar & Jade and PLACE Sports, founded in 1969, with franchise partners operating in about 20 other countries. Mass-market family consumer brand with solid US awareness.

San Francisco online marketplace founded 2008 connecting households with local pros for home services like cleaning, plumbing and moving. Revenue comes from leads paid by professionals. Raised hundreds of millions in funding. It was founded in 2008 by Marco Zappacosta, Jonathan Swanson and Sander Daniels, and a 2021 funding round valued it at about USD 3.2 billion. Consumer brand with national US recognition and TV and sports advertising.

San Francisco consumer goods company selling sustainable household and personal care products direct-to-consumer, including Grove Co. and Seed Phytonutrients. Went public on the NYSE (GROV) via SPAC in 2022 and has shrunk since. Founded in 2012 by Stuart Landesberg, it is a certified B Corp, ships in plastic-free packaging and sells mostly through subscription orders. Consumer brand with modest US awareness.

Chicago-based provider of food processing technology, freezers, fillers and airport ground equipment, listed on the NYSE (JBTM). Acquired Marel in 2025 and renamed JBT Marel. Customers are food, beverage and poultry processors and airports. JBT was spun off from FMC Technologies in 2008. Its JBT AeroTech arm makes airport ground support equipment, and the Marel deal added poultry, meat and fish processing lines. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

US maker of class rings, yearbooks, graduation announcements and school jewellery, based in Minneapolis, selling to high school and college students through schools. Owned by Platinum Equity. Customers are students, schools and parents. Founded in Minnesota in 1897, the firm also makes championship rings for sports teams. Consumer-facing brand known in US education.

Kazakhstan fintech super-app and bank, Kaspi.kz, based in Almaty and offering payments, marketplace shopping and consumer finance to millions of customers. Listed on Nasdaq (KSPI). Acquired Turkish e-commerce firm Hepsiburada. Founders Mikheil Lomtadze and Vyacheslav Kim built it from a bank into a super-app with about 14 million monthly active users, including Kaspi Pay, Kaspi Red instalments and Kaspi Travel. Very high consumer awareness in Kazakhstan.

Singapore-based combat sports promotion founded in 2011, hosting mixed martial arts, Muay Thai and kickboxing events across Asia, broadcast worldwide. Revenue from broadcast rights, sponsorship and tickets. Large Asian fan following and global sponsors. It was founded by Chatri Sityodtong, who is chairman and CEO. ONE Friday Fights runs weekly from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, and ONE Fight Night events air in the US on Amazon Prime Video. High sports sponsorship visibility.

US natural and organic grocery chain from Phoenix, Arizona, with about 450 stores in 24 states, focused on fresh produce and healthy food. Listed on Nasdaq (SFM). Revenue around USD 8 billion. Founded in 2002 in Chandler, Arizona, the chain sells its own Sprouts Brand private label as well as natural and organic brands, and is led by CEO Jack Sinclair. Consumer brand with strong awareness in the US sunbelt.

Alabama-based producer and exporter of metallurgical coal for steelmaking, mining in Alabama, and listed on the NYSE (HCC). Customers are steelmakers in Europe, Asia and Brazil. Mines are Mine 4, Mine 7 and the new Blue Creek development in Tuscaloosa County, formed after the 2015 bankruptcy of Walter Energy and listed in 2017. B2B commodity producer with no consumer awareness.

Malaysian low-cost airline brand founded in 2001 by Tony Fernandes, now under the Capital A group, flying across Asia with about 200 aircraft. Large following, sponsor of football and motorsport. Tony Fernandes and Kamarudin Meranun bought the airline in 2001 for a token sum. Fernandes also ran the Caterham Formula 1 team and the airline sponsored F1 outfits in that period. The AirAsia group, now Capital A, also has the AirAsia Move super-app. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia.

Indonesian investing app for stocks and mutual funds for retail investors, based in Jakarta, backed by Sequoia and Horizons Ventures. Founded in 2018, with millions of users. It was founded in 2018 by Anderson Sumarli and Yada Piyajomkwan, and generates revenue from trading fees and investment products. Moderate consumer awareness in Indonesia.

Taiwanese ASIC design service provider, listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3661), supporting custom chips for AI and high-performance computing for cloud hyperscalers. TSMC is a significant shareholder. Alchip was founded in 2003. Its ASIC design work covers advanced process nodes, and customers are reported to include large US cloud providers developing AI accelerators. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Canadian consumer products group in Montreal behind juvenile brands Maxi-Cosi, Cosco and Safety 1st, and bicycle brands Cannondale and Schwinn, sold through major retailers worldwide. Listed on the TSX (DII.B). Cannondale was sold to Pon Holdings in 2017, so the cycling business now includes Schwinn, GT, Mongoose and Caloi, alongside juvenile brands Quinny, Bebe Confort and Tiger. Strong consumer awareness in children's and cycling products.

Israeli AI and cyber defence company based in Tel Aviv, selling sovereign AI systems that protect critical infrastructure and government networks. Backed by investors. Customers are governments and critical infrastructure operators. It was co-founded by Shalev Hulio, the co-founder of NSO Group, with Gil Dolev, and raised about USD 100 million in 2025 at a valuation around USD 1.1 billion. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Kuwaiti low-cost airline operating scheduled flights from Kuwait to the Middle East, Asia and Europe with Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft. Listed on Boursa Kuwait. Founder Marwan Boodai started it as Kuwait's first private airline in 2004, listing on the Kuwait exchange in 2005. It operates from Terminal 5 at Kuwait International Airport, and also runs Jazeera Terminal Services for ground handling. Strong regional brand awareness.

Qingdao-based operator of one of China's largest EV charging networks, with hundreds of thousands of charging points, a subsidiary of TBEA. Customers are EV drivers and fleets. Teld's network is owned by TBEA, and it also makes charging equipment and supplies energy storage and vehicle-to-grid solutions to grid and fleet customers. Strong awareness among Chinese EV drivers.

US wheel, tire and undercarriage maker in Quincy, Illinois, producing agricultural, construction and mining wheels under the Titan and Goodyear Farm Tires brands. Listed on the NYSE (TWI). Titan International was founded in 1990 as Titan Wheel by Maurice Taylor, and supplies original equipment makers including Deere, CNH and AGCO with large wheels. It has plants in the US, Europe and Brazil. B2B with moderate recognition among farmers.

Helsinki AI cloud provider, formerly DataCrunch, renting GPU capacity and AI infrastructure to developers and enterprises from data centres in Finland. Backed by European investors. DataCrunch, founded in 2019, sells dedicated GPU clusters and serverless inference powered by renewable electricity, mainly with Nvidia chips. B2B with limited public brand awareness.

Michigan electric delivery truck maker, listed on Nasdaq (WKHS), producing the W56 step van and merging with Motiv Electric Trucks in 2025. Customers are fleet buyers. The company was formerly AMP Holding in Ohio, and lost its bid for the US Postal Service's Next Generation Delivery Vehicle contract to Oshkosh in 2021. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

New York neobank for immigrants, letting newcomers get US credit cards and bank accounts using their foreign credit history. Founded in 2020 with funding from Accel and others. It was founded by Raghunandan G, who previously started the cab-hailing start-up TaxiForSure, and Priyadeep Sinha, with a strong India link. Consumer fintech brand with moderate awareness among immigrants.

London core banking software company founded by Antony Jenkins, former Barclays CEO, selling a cloud-native banking platform to banks including JPMorgan Chase's UK digital bank. Other banks using the platform include Westpac in Australia, and JPMorgan's Chase UK was built on it. The company is based in London. B2B software with little public awareness.

London AI compliance and surveillance firm that helps banks monitor communications and detect misconduct. Founded in 2014 and backed by SoftBank and General Atlantic. It was founded by Erkin Adylov and sells its AI compliance products to global investment banks and regulators' regulated firms. B2B software with limited public awareness.

Bengaluru-based trucking platform offering a freight marketplace, fuel cards and payments for truck operators. Raised funding from Tiger Global and Accel and listed on Indian exchanges in 2025. The company is formally Zinka Logistics Solutions, founded in 2015 by Rajesh Yabaji, Chanakya Hridaya and Ramasubramanian B, and listed in India in November 2025. B2B with strong awareness among truckers.

Tokyo-based manufacturing procurement and AI data platform helping companies source made-to-order parts and drawings. Founded in 2017 and backed by Japanese and global investors. Founder Yushiro Kato, a former McKinsey consultant, set it up in 2017 and its main product is CADDi Drawer, which organises engineering drawings with AI. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Austin-based fabless chip maker supplying audio codecs and haptic drivers for phones and laptops, with Apple as its largest customer. Listed on Nasdaq (CRUS). Revenue about USD 1.9 billion. It acquired Scottish chipmaker Wolfson Microelectronics in 2014 and keeps a design centre in Edinburgh. Apple accounts for the large majority of sales. B2B with no consumer visibility.

US payment card manufacturer in Littleton, Colorado, producing credit, debit and prepaid cards for banks and fintechs. Listed on Nasdaq (PMTS). The firm makes EMV chip and contactless cards, and its Card@Once instant issuance system lets banks print cards in branches. It was founded in 1983 in Colorado. B2B with no consumer brand.

Shenzhen-based humanoid robot developer EngineAI, making humanoid robots such as the SE01 and PM01. Founded in 2023. Customers include research, industrial and entertainment clients. Founder Zhao Tongyang started the company in 2023, and its humanoids include the SA01 and the full-size T800 showcased in 2025. Viral robot demonstrations have given it brand visibility in China.

London talent investor that recruits technical founders, builds teams and funds early start-ups. Founded in 2011 by Alice Bentinck and Matt Clifford. Alumni companies include Tractable, Cleo and Magic Pony, which Twitter bought in 2016. It runs programmes in London, Paris, Berlin, Bangalore, Singapore and the US. B2B investor, known in the tech community.

Singapore-based arm of the Taiwanese financial holding Fubon, which offers life insurance in Asia. The parent Fubon Financial is listed in Taiwan. Fubon Financial Holding also owns Taipei Fubon Bank, Fubon Insurance and Fubon Securities, and sponsors Taiwanese professional baseball and basketball teams. Consumer insurance brand with strong awareness in Taiwan.

Pittsburgh robotics firm using wall-climbing robots to inspect boilers, pipelines and tanks for industrial customers. Founded in 2013 and raised significant funding at a high valuation. The firm was founded by Jake Loosararian, passed the USD 1 billion valuation mark in 2022, and counts US Navy and power utilities as customers through its Thoro.ai analytics. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

San Francisco data and AI marketing platform that syncs a company's data warehouse with marketing tools and runs AI marketing agents. Customers include large brands. Founders Tejas Manohar, Kashish Gupta and Josh Curl created the reverse ETL category and now sell a composable customer data platform. B2B software with strong standing among data teams.

IDB Invest, the private-sector arm of the Inter-American Development Bank, headquartered in Washington, lending to companies in Latin America and the Caribbean. Formerly the Inter-American Investment Corporation, it was founded in 1986 and rebranded in 2017. It is rated AAA and owned by member countries. Multilateral development institution with no consumer brand.

UK specialist retirement income provider based in Reigate, Surrey, offering annuities and lifetime mortgages. Previously listed on the LSE (JUST) and taken over by Brookfield in 2025. It was formed by the 2016 merger of Just Retirement and Partnership Assurance, and Brookfield's takeover in 2025 was valued at about GBP 2.4 billion. Consumer brand with moderate UK awareness.

Chip development company spun out of NIO, the Chinese premium electric vehicle maker, designing automotive and industrial chips including smart driving silicon. Supplies mainly NIO vehicles. Its NX9031 chip, built on a 5nm process, was announced in 2024 for NIO's ET9 flagship sedan. B2B with limited public brand awareness; parent NIO is a well-known consumer EV brand.

Oxford-based UK autonomous vehicle software company, spun out of Oxford University, supplying driverless systems for industrial vehicles, buses and trucks. Customers include airports, mines and logistics firms. Previously Oxbotica. Founders Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner started the business in 2014. Its Oxa Driver software is installed on shuttles and airport vehicles. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Connecticut-based mail, shipping and e-commerce technology company, the long-time postage meter maker, selling mailing and shipping equipment, software and financial services. Listed on NYSE (PBI), founded 1920. Customers are businesses and governments. Founded in 1920 by Arthur Pitney and Walter Bowes, it exited the Global Ecommerce parcel business in 2024 and now concentrates on SendTech mailing products and Presort services. Well-known business brand.

Poland's major mobile network operator Play, with over 15 million subscribers, offering mobile, internet and TV, owned by Iliad Group of France. Warsaw-based. Play launched in 2007, and Iliad bought it in 2020 and added the cable provider UPC Polska in 2022. Very high consumer awareness in Poland, with sports sponsorship.

Tokyo AI research lab founded in 2023 by former Google researchers, developing nature-inspired foundation models and the AI Scientist. Valued above USD 2 billion. Backed by Japanese banks and global investors. Co-founders David Ha and Llion Jones, an author of the Transformer paper, run the lab, and MUFG has partnered on financial AI. It focuses on evolutionary and nature-inspired methods. Research and B2B brand with growing visibility in Japan.

French IT services and consulting group, formed by Sopra and Steria in 2014, with about 56,000 staff and revenue of around EUR 5.8 billion. Based in Paris area. Listed on Euronext Paris (SOP). Sopra Steria also includes Sopra Banking Software, and the Pasquier family remains a significant shareholder. It operates mostly in France, the UK, Germany and the Nordics. B2B digital services with sports sponsorship in rugby and cycling visibility.

London-based generative AI company behind the Stable Diffusion image models, selling model access to creators and enterprises. Founded 2019 by Emad Mostaque. Reported troubled finances in 2023-24, then restructuring. Stable Diffusion appeared in 2022, with Stable Video and Stable Audio later. CEO Prem Akkaraju took over from Mostaque in 2024, and film director James Cameron joined the board. Brand recognised among AI users; a notable name in AI.

Japanese space start-up in Tokyo operating StriX synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites that provide Earth observation data for governments and businesses. Founded 2018. Listed on Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market in 2023. Founder Motoyuki Arai set up the company in 2018, and the listing actually took place in December 2024. Customers include Japanese government agencies. B2B with low consumer awareness.

UK connected vehicle data company that collected car data, listed on Nasdaq in 2021 via SPAC and filed for bankruptcy in 2023. Defunct. Customers were carmakers and mapping firms. The company, founded by Richard Barlow in 2014, listed in November 2021 through a SPAC merger and filed for insolvency protection in May 2023. General Motors was an early investor. No consumer visibility.

Chan Zuckerberg Biohub network research institute in the US using AI, imaging and biology to understand disease. Nonprofit research body. In 2025 the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative reorganised its science effort around Biohub and bought the AI-biology firm EvolutionaryScale, with Alex Rives as head of science. No commercial sponsorship role but has high profile in science.

California edge AI chip and software company, listed on Nasdaq (BZAI) via a 2025 SPAC merger with BurTech, selling processors for vision AI in automotive, defence and retail. Blaize was formerly Thinci, founded in 2010, and its architecture is called the Graph Streaming Processor. It completed a SPAC deal with BurTech in January 2025. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

US AI drug discovery firm (Genesis Therapeutics) renamed Genesis Molecular AI, using AI to design small-molecule drugs with pharma partners. Based in California. Founder Evan Feinberg leads the firm, which has partnered with Incyte and Genentech, and its Pearl model predicts how drugs bind proteins. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Electric motorcycle maker spun out of Harley-Davidson, building the LiveWire S2 Del Mar and One electric bikes. Listed on NYSE (LVWR) via SPAC in 2022 and majority held by Harley-Davidson. The S2 Del Mar and S2 Mulholland are built at Harley-Davidson's York plant in Pennsylvania. Consumer premium brand with moderate awareness among motorbike fans.

Australian-founded maker of DC fast chargers for electric vehicles, once listed on Nasdaq (DCFC), whose assets were bought by India's Exicom in 2024. Tritium was founded in 2001 in Brisbane and sold its Veefil chargers worldwide. It entered administration in January 2024, and Exicom bought it later that year. It listed through a SPAC in 2022. B2B charger supplier.

Spanish Earth intelligence start-up, founded in 2024, that combines satellite data and AI to produce insights for businesses and governments. Customers pay for data products. Backed by European investors. CEO Fabrizio Pirondini leads it, and L3Harris is building the satellite sensors. B2B space and data company with no consumer awareness; based in Madrid.

Munich-based robotics company producing robot arms and AI-driven robot systems for manufacturing and labs, with funding from investors such as Sequoia. Customers are industrial and research firms, and it has operations in Germany and China. Founded in 2018 by Zhaopeng Chen and Peter Meusel, it bought the assets of Franka Emika, maker of Franka robot arms, in 2023. B2B robotics brand with low consumer awareness.

Spanish independent investment bank and asset manager based in Madrid, with M&A advisory, credit portfolio and asset management arms, and offices across Europe, the US and Asia. Customers are companies and institutional investors. Alantra, originally N+1, is listed in Madrid under ALNT and its chairman is Santiago Eguidazu. B2B financial advisory firm with low consumer awareness.

Hong Kong's flagship airline, Cathay Pacific, flying to over 80 destinations with a hub at Hong Kong International Airport. Owned by Swire, Air China and Qatar Airways; listed on HKEX (293). Cathay was founded in 1946, and Swire holds roughly 45 percent. It also runs HK Express, bought in 2019, and cargo airline Air Hong Kong. It sponsors the Hong Kong Sevens. High-visibility consumer brand and prior sports sponsor including rugby sevens.

US semiconductor equipment subsystem maker based in Fremont, California, making fluid delivery systems for chip tool makers like Lam and Applied Materials. Listed on Nasdaq (ICHR). Ichor was founded in 1999, and its customers include Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA. It also operates plants in Malaysia and Singapore. B2B with no consumer awareness.

LiDAR maker for autonomous vehicles, founded in Silicon Valley with big China operations, supplying sensors to NIO and others, and merged into Seyond with Hong Kong listing plans. Seyond is the 2023 rebrand, and its Falcon lidar is in NIO's ET7. A Hong Kong SPAC route was announced in 2024. B2B with low consumer awareness.

US cloud hosting platform for developers, used to deploy web apps, databases and scheduled jobs, positioned as a simpler alternative to the large cloud providers. Based in San Francisco. Customers are developers and software teams paying for usage. Founded in 2018 by Anurag Goel, formerly of Stripe, it is a popular alternative to Heroku. B2B with awareness in developer communities.

Canadian-listed (Nasdaq: ANY) bitcoin mining and data hosting company that was formerly known for virtual desktop and data storage products. Customers were enterprises and its revenue now comes mainly from mining. It acquired Overland Storage in 2014, the origin of the Overland-Tandberg storage business. Small-cap B2B firm with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

US robotics company based in New York building AI-enabled industrial robot arms for manufacturing, such as machine tending and assembly. Customers are manufacturers who buy or lease the robots. Founded in 2020 and backed by venture investors. Its RO1 robot arm was developed by CEO Evan Beard. B2B with low consumer awareness.

US clinical AI voice assistant for doctors that automates note-taking and fills in electronic health records during patient visits. Based in California. Customers are hospitals and physician groups paying subscriptions. Founded in 2016 by Punit Soni, a former Google and Motorola executive, its Suki Assistant listens to consultations and writes notes. B2B healthcare software with no consumer awareness.

Canadian automation platform company based in Montreal, offering a browser-based design tool and on-demand parts and software for building industrial automation and robot cells. Customers are manufacturers and integrators. Founder Etienne Lacroix started it in 2016 and its hardware is branded MachineMotion. B2B technology firm with growing awareness in engineering.

US enterprise carbon accounting and climate platform based in San Francisco, used by large companies such as Walmart and Airbnb to measure emissions and set sustainability targets. Revenue comes from software subscriptions. Watershed was founded in 2019 by Taylor Francis and Christian Anderson, and a 2024 round valued it at USD 1.8 billion. B2B with no consumer awareness but a strong name among sustainability teams.

US autonomous security testing start-up whose AI agent has ranked at the top of bug bounty leaderboards. Customers are companies that want continuous penetration testing, paying software subscriptions. Founded in 2024 and backed by notable investors. Founder Oege de Moor previously created GitHub's code analysis tool Semmle. B2B with niche recognition in cybersecurity.

Brazilian cosmetics and beauty group, owner of Natura, Avon, The Body Shop and Aesop. Direct-selling model with millions of consultants. Based in Sao Paulo, listed on B3 (NATU3). Now named Natura Cosmeticos, the group sold Aesop to L'Oreal in 2023 and The Body Shop to Aurelius that year. Avon Products went through a US Chapter 11 process in 2024. Strong global consumer brands.

Canadian e-commerce platform serving millions of merchants, and the leading commerce software for online stores. Ottawa-based, listed on TSX and Nasdaq (SHOP). Revenue about USD 9 billion. Shopify was founded in 2006 by Tobi Lutke and sells Shopify Plus to large merchants, with Shop Pay as its checkout wallet. It is a regular name in Formula 1 paddock partnerships. Known in business and tech, and has held Formula 1 team sponsorship deals.

Renault Group's sports car and Formula 1 brand, based in Dieppe and Viry-Chatillon, making the A110 and Alpenglow and running the Alpine F1 team. Consumer premium sports car brand with strong motorsport visibility. Alpine was founded in 1955 by Jean Redele in Dieppe, and the brand's models include the A110, the A290 hatchback and the A390 coupe SUV. Already in F1.

US food company, Marzetti, owner of Marzetti dressings, Sister Schubert's rolls and other brands, formerly Lancaster Colony; Columbus, Ohio. Listed on Nasdaq (MZTI). Its licensed products include Chick-fil-A and Olive Garden dressings, and other brands are New York BRAND Bakery and Flatout. Founded in 1961 by John Gerlach. Consumer brand with national retail reach.

German department store chain Galeria, formerly Galeria Karstadt Kaufhof, with about 80 stores selling fashion, beauty and household goods. It went through insolvency twice, in 2020 and 2022 and 2023. Customers are German shoppers. Galeria sought insolvency protection in 2020, 2022 and January 2024, and was taken over in 2024 by Richard Baker and Bernd Beetz after the collapse of owner Signa. Consumer retail brand with strong awareness in Germany.

US-listed mining company, Critical Metals Corp, developing the Tanbreez rare earths project in Greenland, listed on Nasdaq (CRML). Customers would be buyers of rare earth materials used in magnets and electronics. It owns 92.5 percent of the Tanbreez deposit in southern Greenland and the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria. Pre-production resource company with no consumer awareness.

Retro gaming hardware company, ModRetro, founded by Palmer Luckey, selling retro console products such as the Chromatic handheld. Customers are enthusiast gamers who buy online. Palmer Luckey also founded Oculus VR and the defence company Anduril. ModRetro makes the M64 N64-style console as well. Niche consumer brand with a loyal following and attention-grabbing founder.

US casual dining chain, Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, headquartered in Greenwood Village, Colorado, with about 500 restaurants. Listed on Nasdaq (RRGB). Customers are families. The chain began in Seattle in 1969 and is known for bottomless steak fries, with franchised restaurants in the US and Canada. Consumer brand known in the US.

Australian fruit and vegetable canning and food company, SPC, formerly Shepparton Preserving Company, based in Victoria. It sells canned fruit, baked beans and spaghetti to consumers and retailers. SPC dates from 1917 in the Goulburn Valley and owns the Ardmona fruit brand. Consumer food brand with high awareness in Australia.

Specialty metals and advanced materials group, AMG, based in Netherlands, though HQ listed as US in input. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (AMG). AMG now trades as AMG Critical Materials, with units in lithium, vanadium, titanium and furnace engineering, based in Amsterdam. Customers are in aerospace, steel and battery industries. B2B.

Russian truck maker KAMAZ, based in Naberezhnye Chelny, famous for its Dakar Rally winning trucks and for heavy trucks and buses in Russia and former Soviet markets. State-linked group. Rostec is the largest shareholder, and the KAMAZ-master team has won the Dakar Rally many times. Strong brand in Russia and in motorsport.

Swedish Volvo Group, maker of Volvo trucks, buses and construction equipment, Mack and Renault Trucks, based in Gothenburg. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Revenue about SEK 550 billion. Separate from Volvo Cars. Brands include Renault Trucks, Mack, UD Trucks, Prevost, Nova Bus and Volvo Penta marine engines. Volvo Cars was sold to Ford in 1999. Strong B2B brand, sponsor of sports.

Italian automotive gas fuel systems maker Landi Renzo, in Cavriago, listed on Borsa Italiana (LR), producing LPG, methane and hydrogen fuel systems for vehicles. Customers are car makers and aftermarket buyers worldwide. Founded in 1954, it has a family holding behind it, and owns the SAFE&CEC compressor business. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

US cell tower real estate investment trust from Boston, owning about 150,000 communication sites worldwide, leased to mobile operators. Listed on the NYSE (AMT). The company was founded in 1995, owns data centres through CoreSite (bought in 2021), and counts AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon as tenants. It also operates in India, Africa, Europe and Latin America. B2B infrastructure owner with no consumer brand.

Copper is a London-based digital asset custody and technology firm, founded in 2018, providing institutional crypto custody, prime brokerage and settlement networks (ClearLoop) for funds and exchanges. Customers are institutions. Crunchbase shows about $281 million in funding. Founder Dmitry Tokarev leads the company. B2B crypto infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Runway Growth Capital is a US specialty finance company, a business development company based in Woodside, California (the input lists New York), that provides loans to venture-backed growth-stage companies. It is listed on Nasdaq (RWAY). Runway Growth Capital manages it, and the fund listed in 2021. Financial vehicle with no consumer brand awareness.

Atom Computing is a US quantum computing company based in Berkeley, California, building gate-based quantum computers using neutral atoms trapped by lasers. It partners with Microsoft on error-corrected systems and has raised about 191 million dollars. Atom Computing worked with Microsoft to entangle 24 logical qubits in late 2024, and a machine called Magne is planned in Denmark. B2B and research-focused with no consumer brand awareness.

Helm.ai is a US autonomous driving software company based in Redwood City, California, developing AI software for advanced driver assistance and self-driving systems, selling to automakers such as Honda. It has raised about 165 million dollars. Founded in 2016 by Vlad Voroninski and Tudor Achim, with Honda an investor and customer. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

RobCo is a German robotics company based in Munich that makes modular robot arms and AI software for flexible industrial automation, aimed at small and mid-sized manufacturers. It has raised about 160 million dollars. Its RobCo Studio software programs the robot arms without code. B2B with awareness among manufacturers and none among consumers.

Dash0 is a US observability company based in New York (with a European engineering team) offering an OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for monitoring software systems. It has raised about 155 million dollars per the input. Its founder Mirko Novakovic previously created Instana, sold to IBM. B2B developer tooling with no consumer brand awareness.

Ocient is a US data analytics company based in Chicago that sells a hyperscale data warehouse for analysing very large datasets, used by telecoms, adtech and government customers. It has raised about 157 million dollars. Founded by Chris Gladwin, who earlier created Cleversafe, sold to IBM. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Hua Xia Bank is a Chinese joint-stock commercial bank, based in Beijing, founded in 1992 with Shougang Group as an early backer, offering corporate, retail and financial markets banking through branches nationwide. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600015). Hua Xia lists the State Grid and PICC alongside Shougang as major shareholders. Moderate domestic consumer recognition.

Accolade is a US personalised health and benefits navigation company, based in Seattle, offering employers expert support, advocacy and virtual care for employees. Listed on Nasdaq (ACCD) in 2020 and acquired by Transcarent in 2025. It bought the telehealth firm PlushCare in 2022, and Transcarent's takeover closed in 2025. B2B2C with limited consumer visibility.

Xendit is an Indonesian payments infrastructure fintech, founded in 2015 and based in Jakarta, which provides payment gateways, disbursements and business accounts for companies across Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia. Customers include merchants and platforms. Founders Moses Lo and Zac Ong started Xendit. B2B with low consumer profile.

Australian blockchain gaming company based in Sydney, behind Immutable X, Immutable Passport and games like Gods Unchained, Guild of Guardians and Immutable Play. Revenue from platform fees and token holdings, with investors including Tencent and Temasek. Founded in 2018. Founders James and Robbie Ferguson run the company, which also runs the Immutable zkEVM network. Known mainly among web3 gamers.

Pasadena-based location data intelligence SaaS platform operating as Near, which collects consumer movement and mobile data for marketing and analytics. Went public via SPAC in 2023, then filed for bankruptcy in December 2023. Founder Anil Mathews built the Allspark platform, and it merged with KludeIn in March 2023. B2B data company, mainly known to advertisers.

New York-based identity verification and authentication company (formerly Payfone), using phone-number based signals to verify customers for banks, fintechs and retailers. Revenue from per-verification fees. Venture-funded with about $251 million raised. Pre-Fill is its best-known product, and it adopted the Prove name after Payfone acquired Prove in 2021. B2B brand, known in financial services identity.

Chinese state-owned power equipment maker based in Shanghai, listed in Shanghai (601727) and Hong Kong (2727), making thermal, wind, nuclear and grid equipment and industrial services. One of China's largest equipment groups. It owns a minority stake in the Italian power equipment maker Ansaldo Energia. B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

Japanese flying car developer in Toyota City, Aichi, working on eVTOL aircraft for passengers and cargo, founded in 2018, supported by Toyota affiliates and Suzuki. Demonstrated at Osaka Expo 2025. Founder Tomohiro Fukuzawa leads it, and its SD-05 aircraft is a two-seat eVTOL. Pre-commercial startup, with growing press attention in Japan.

Calgary-based natural gas and condensate producer, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TOU), and Canada's largest gas producer, mainly in Alberta's Montney and Deep Basin. Revenue from commodity sales. CEO Mike Rose started the business in 2008, with output over half a million barrels of oil equivalent a day. B2B energy company, little consumer brand awareness.

Indian online travel company based in Gurugram, listed on Nasdaq (YTRA), selling flights, hotels, holidays and corporate travel services to consumers and businesses. Founded in 2006 and active across India. Corporate travel is its largest segment. Yatra listed through a 2016 SPAC merger with Terrapin 3. Consumer-facing travel brand with solid recognition in India.

San Francisco-based active metadata and data collaboration platform helping data teams catalog, govern and understand data assets, serving customers such as enterprises and tech firms. Founded in 2020 in India and venture-funded with about $200 million raised. Founders Prukalpa Sankar and Varun Banka lead it. B2B software brand, known in data engineering.

Pleasanton, California-based cyber insurance provider for small and mid-size businesses, using AI risk assessment to underwrite policies through brokers. Founded in 2019, venture-funded with about $208 million. Founders Jack Kudale and Rajeev Gupta lead the business, and its policies are branded Cowbell Prime. Insurance brand known to brokers and SME owners in the US.

Regulated water utility headquartered in San Dimas, California, serving about 1 million people across Southern and Northern California. A subsidiary of American States Water (NYSE: AWR). Revenue from regulated water rates. It serves customers in about 80 communities in ten counties and provides electricity in Big Bear Lake through Bear Valley Electric. Local utility brand with little sponsorship use.
